speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) to date, how many seniors have been engaged through the Seniors Go Digital Programme; and (b) whether the Ministry has plans to enhance or put in place more programmes to specifically target online scams against seniors.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) whether those who participated in the Seniors Go Digital Programme are now more proficient in using digital devices in their daily lives, such as to access Singpass, online booking of polyclinic appointments and checking of account balances; and (b) beyond numbers, whether the focus of the Programme can be to improve digital usage by seniors going forward.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) understands that going digital can be a daunting experience.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is one reason we established the SG Digital Office (SDO) in June 2020, to better support people who need help, such as seniors, hawkers and heartland merchants, with basic digital tools and skills.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The programme focuses on training and enabling seniors to use digital tools for their daily lives.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These include using a smartphone to access Government services like Singpass and health services, and to communicate and transact online.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Targeted programmes have also been implemented to strengthen seniors' ability to manage cyber threats.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The programmes I mentioned are regularly reviewed and updated to ensure their relevance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Singapore Police Force (SPF) and National Crime Prevention Council (NCPC) have also rolled out broad-based and targeted public education efforts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These include the annual anti-scam public education campaign, "Spot the Signs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Stop the Crimes.", which builds awareness and vigilance amongst the general public on the tell-tale signs of scams.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: NCPC's Volunteer Crime Prevention Ambassadors also engage residents, including seniors, to share crime prevention tips.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Complementing the Government's programmes, the Digital for Life (DfL) movement was launched in 2021 to galvanise the support of people, private and public (3P) sectors on ground-up initiatives to help Singaporeans gain confidence in going digital.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, at the Majestic Smart Seniors Applied Centre, managed by RSVP Singapore, seniors learn to identify and avoid scams, and protect their digital identity through curated modules and webinars conducted in partnership with Google.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Government continuously reviews its anti-scam programmes and efforts to ensure they are updated and relevant.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will also continue to work with the community and industry to engage seniors, to help them stay safe and secure online.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The Minister has mentioned that there are 190,000 seniors that were trained.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This is quite an achievement since it started, because over the first year, it was only 100,000.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Are there any specific targets that the Ministry has set for us to train as many seniors as we can?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The second question is, there are three tiers of digital competency for the seniors, with scams being one of the largest threats to seniors, especially now that they are coming on board.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Is there a need to enhance tier three of the competency, or to introduce a new tier of competency so that seniors are always protected as they come on board the digital training?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But to your question, is there a target number?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think we are also very cognisant of the fact that seniors tend to take a longer time to become familiar with the digital domain and they would want to gain confidence a step at a time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we would not want to rush the seniors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We also do not want the seniors to feel that the only way they can have a meaningful life is to engage digitally.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are other things that are meaningful, but adding the digital dimension can help them to keep in touch with their friends through new means; to plug into opportunities for recreation, for understanding the world and to engage with society in a way that they could not have done so before.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But it is important to note that we should let them take it at their own pace.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Right now, we have organised some of the programmes according to tiers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I should also add that, in fact, once they gain confidence in going digital, some of the seniors are very savvy.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are so good that they can teach their friends how to become more effective.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And then the question becomes: how are they able to learn new knowledge to teach their friends?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In fact, through online resources, they are already able to become even more competent.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, that would be the approach that we take.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is also not just the programmes that matter.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think there are many touch points that seniors can come into contact with, and we do not want to assume that it is only the Government who can provide programmes that will work and be effective.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Crowding in the partners is equally important, because it is also a question of building trust with the seniors, so that they are receptive to what is being shared with them.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: For example, how to use Singpass, calling a cab, ordering food, TeleConsult and so on.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And if I may come back to my Parliamentary Question, on the polyclinic appointment bookings.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: With COVID-19 cases still high, the polyclinics are obviously very busy with high numbers of visits.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Many of the seniors were told to book online and there are only limited walk-ins that you can book, but they are feeling helpless about how they can make a booking through the online platforms and how to go through the whole process – including using a Singpass, Singnet profiles and so on.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Can I ask the Minister, if the digital office could also look at how to assist seniors to help them in some of these functions for their daily lives?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The first module is on connectivity and communication.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And yet another module on entertainment, MeLISTEN, MeWATCH and using NLB's Libby app.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, there is quite a range of things.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In particular, there are several other features that would be of particular use to our seniors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But again, it all depends on the seniors' comfort level and what they find to be useful.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I should just add that, inherent in Mr Liang's question is also a tension.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is a tension in wanting to help the seniors become more familiar with a range of digital applications and so nudging them in that direction to use digital services, as a motivation for them to learn about the tools and how to go digital.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And on the other hand, recognising that some of these seniors will find this a very difficult task and they might actually feel very anxious.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, between the two, we have to find the right balance and try to move things forward.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They may not be as convenient as the digital avenues, but it does not mean that seniors do not have the non-digital options available to them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The CDC vouchers is a very good example.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Many seniors over time have learnt and gained confidence on how to use the digital vouchers, but there remains a group that far prefers to use the physical vouchers and those options still remain visible.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In summary, we will continue to nudge forward, and we will continue to offer options for seniors who feel more confident and want to move to the next level of their digital engagement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But we will also want to be very mindful that some seniors are still not yet comfortable, and we want to offer them that sense of confidence that they are not being pushed in a direction that they do not wish to go.
